summary: Read all 14 bodies including both bundle/chain versions, five generated preamble variants, contextual README snippets and the workspace example. Typed inherited properties and once-owned setup are appropriate. Revise an obsolete prop-import workaround and excessive historical comments, reconcile the runnable transcript with its evolved sidecars, and investigate chain/camera behavior on a second launch. Runtime results cited in existing prose were not reproduced by this review.

lenses.smells_idioms: Renderer -> bundle -> chain -> modes connections in build.yaml supply inherited typed values; no raw property access or thisBox aliases. once.bundle keeps expensive setup stable. Suspected rerun defects concern addPassChain input capture and camera target mutation, not missing sleeps or graph topology.
lenses.imports: Explicit fabricated imports are meaningful because that package is not in automatic imports. props.kt propTypeImports now carries matching local imports into the preamble, invalidating the leading workaround comment. No deterministic analyzer report was present in this assigned packet; no import removals are proposed. Coordinator should run the established analyzer for redundant math imports; do not infer unused imports from generated preambles.
lenses.whitespace: Renderer and mode bodies have readable short groups. Keep the four-mode comment table aligned. Sidecar chain has 59 comment lines among 108 total lines, placing controls below a long implementation history; move controls together near the top and reduce history. Generated preambles are generator output, not hand-formatting targets.
lenses.comments: Retain the useful persistent-pixels versus frameHistory-correspondence distinction, equal-resolution requirement and row-major handle ordering. Remove the obsolete prop bug explanation; replace the chain saturation/yaw/dolly history with concise current units and why objects move. Pure yaw is depth-independent but does not imply spatially constant perspective flow.
lenses.glsl: No shader source in these 14 bodies. temporalAccumulate/temporalDebug obtain generated GLSL from FabricatePassLibrary; reviewed perPixelMotion=true defaults, previousUv-currentUv convention, named display mode push and frameHistory flags in that implementation. No generated GLSL layout edits proposed.
lenses.live_coding: No authored fragment markers or declaration/assignment reset pairs occur in these bodies. Preserve once setup and the modes loop. chain uses typed reassignment for rebuilds, but the API captures the current final post target before name replacement; verify second launch. Sidecar t/yawApplied are fresh per launch while camera object persists, and setting camera.at without preserving target-at deserves a deterministic pose check.
lenses.helpers: Checked Already in Field, Approved and Declined sections. Keep explicit attachTo/present calls: self-attaching addPassChain and default fabricated imports were declined. Reuse repaired prop import propagation with short nested type names after compilation. No new helper proposal is needed.

findings.issue: Suspected behavior defect from source reading: FabricatePassChainBuilder.addPassChain captures postStack.output() before replacing existing taa/display effects; FabricatePostStack.output() returns the last target. On a second launch the new taa can therefore take the prior display output as CHAIN_INPUT rather than the original lit scene, while those named targets are reused. No GPU rerun was performed.
findings.proposed_change: Verify the second-launch input identity. If confirmed, fix the chain replacement API to preserve its original upstream input when replacing the same named chain, and retain its persistent-target reuse. Keep explicit attachment/presentation; do not add manual teardown to the teaching box.
findings.verification: Launch renderer/bundle/chain/modes, inspect bound chain input and post-stack ordering, rerun chain twice after changing blend, and capture beauty/debug modes for feedback, stale-source or scheduling errors. Assert the replacement input remains the upstream scene target.

findings.issue: Suspected pose/rerun defect: Camera.yaw(false) rotates target about at. This loop then overwrites at each frame while retaining the old target, so target-at does not preserve the intended orientation under translation. On relaunch yawApplied resets to zero while once.bundle retains the mutated target. The claimed bounded pure-yaw excursion is not established by this source.
findings.proposed_change: Derive both camera position and target from one stable base pose and current time (or preserve a captured view direction while translating); establish that base pose consistently on rerun and invalidate frame history for the intentional cut. Keep the authored temporal reset behavior explicit.
findings.verification: Sample at/target/up across a full dolly cycle and after repeated launches at different phases. Verify target-at direction and yaw bounds, inspect all four modes, and confirm the grid stays in view without cumulative camera drift.

findings.issue: Body 6 in the runnable build transcript still applies unbounded incremental yaw and has no object animation; sidecar body 14 animates saved balls and bounded yaw/dolly, and sidecar body 13 exports balls absent from build body 5. Replaying the advertised transcript therefore creates a materially different lesson and can turn away from the scene. This discrepancy is confirmed by reading the two bodies, not by running them.
findings.proposed_change: Choose the current intended moving-object demonstration, update the authored build bodies consistently with the sidecar source, and regenerate document/metadata through the normal demo workflow. Preserve all graph connections. Hand off README mode expectations, which still describe only uniform camera motion.
findings.verification: Replay the revised build into a fresh disposable document and separately reopen the saved document. Compare box code and inherited balls/preamble state, observe the scene through at least a complete mode cycle and a full camera cycle, and capture modes 0-3.

summary: Read all seven mesh bodies and the transcript execution context. Keep the CPU geometry demonstrations, aligned comparison data and final-expression visualizer gesture. Reuse an existing FLine path idiom, correct specific comment/label overclaims and consolidate the previously approved measurement helpers as follow-up work. No execution or capture was performed; numeric and visual claims remain checks for the edit pass.

lenses.smells_idioms: Pure-compute boxes create independent meshes and display through showMeshGrid or final TriMesh value; no renderer lookup, raw properties, aliases, external event handlers or retained coroutine ownership. SDF definitions precede expensive marching. Existing explicit labels carry teaching information, so automatic showMeshGrid labels would discard useful detail.
lenses.imports: There are no explicit import statements in these seven bodies. Standard math/mesh functions rely on the box intro. No import rewrite or new blanket import is proposed; coordinator owns deterministic evidence if this changes.
lenses.whitespace: Keep (label,mesh) row groups, comparison format columns, named SDF intermediates and grouped showMeshGrid entries. Do not flatten the authored pair tables. The explicit loop/build stages make large bodies navigable; only the FLine first-point branch has a direct existing idiom replacement.
lenses.comments: Most comments explain topology, analytic reference values or the intended editing gesture. Revise the exact ±9% noise label, qualify Taubin volume preservation, and replace absolute Gauss-Bonnet/BVH guarantees with the actual checks/acceleration they provide. Inline visualizer explanation matches mesh_field.kt current 40k/20k behavior; retain final-expression instructions.
lenses.glsl: No GLSL or embedded shaders. These are CPU TriMesh/SDF/Voronoi and rasterized output examples; do not replace them with GPU placeholders. The value card and showMeshGrid use the actual mesh rasterizer.
lenses.live_coding: No //%- fragment markers or declaration/assignment reset pairs occur. Preserve final drilled expression in body 7, since it triggers the value card; retain the printed suggestion to evaluate drilled.flipped(). Per-box rerun recomputes seeded geometry and updates output; runtime determinism and visible refresh were not tested here.
lenses.helpers: Already in Field includes FLine.breakNext()/data("m l+",points), applicable to body 6. Explicit showMeshGrid labels add detail and should remain. Approved compare, mesh.integrate, randomPoints and decimal formatting helpers cover repeated body 1/5/6 measurement scaffolding; record them as approved follow-ups, not new API requests. Declined mesh sizing/dispatch/physics helpers do not apply.

findings.issue: The helix path repeats a first-point conditional that the existing FLine breakNext helper directly expresses; this exact family is listed under Already in Field.
findings.proposed_change: Call path.breakNext() before the unchanged point-generation loop, then path.lineTo(p) for every point, preserving the 121 samples and their order. Keep the point formula readable.
findings.verification: Replay mesh_bridges and compare the path node count/coordinates, tube topology/volume and output image with the original; confirm one initial MoveTo and 120 LineTo nodes.

findings.issue: The scale expression at line 284 is 1 + (u - 0.5) * 0.18, which spans -9% to +9% radial perturbation, not a +18% increase. This is an arithmetic reading, not an observed random sample range.
findings.proposed_change: Label this ±9% radial noise or 18% peak-to-peak radial noise. Keep the seeded expression unchanged unless intentionally revising the study.
findings.verification: Confirm the label against the exact scale formula; replay the process box and inspect the labelled comparison grid.

findings.snippet: mu pair alternates a shrink with an inflate and holds the volume.
findings.issue: Taubin smoothing reduces shrinkage but does not constrain volume exactly. mesh_process.kt implements two smoothingPass calls without volume normalization and documents approximate preservation for the default pair. The teaching prose and volume-held labels overstate what is measured.
findings.proposed_change: Say reduces shrinkage or approximately preserves volume, qualify the related printed annotation/grid label, and keep the measured clean/noisy/laplacian/taubin volumes available for comparison.
findings.verification: Replay mesh_process with the original seed and parameters; report relative volume changes and inspect the smoothing grid before making any stronger quantitative claim.

findings.snippet: // surface is 2 pi times its Euler characteristic. No local bug survives it.
findings.issue: Gauss-Bonnet checks an aggregate, not every local curvature value. gaussianCurvature() divides local angle deficits by mixedVertexAreas(); multiplying by those same areas can cancel local area errors in this sum, so a local bug can survive the demonstrated identity.
findings.proposed_change: Describe this as a global consistency check and retain the separate sphere pointwise/mean comparison. Do not claim that the integral validates all local curvature values.
findings.verification: Read the revised comment against gaussianCurvature()/mixedVertexAreas(); replay and compare the integral and sphere estimates without treating a passing global integral as proof of every local value.

findings.snippet: // The BVH turns every useful query from O(n) into O(log n).
findings.issue: The absolute complexity claim is stronger than the implementation. closestPoint traverses/prunes nodes and can visit many leaves; contains performs multiple parity rays and raycastAll repeatedly calls raycast. These implementations provide acceleration without an unconditional O(log n) bound for every query.
findings.proposed_change: State that a BVH prunes spatially irrelevant triangles and speeds repeated ray/nearest queries. Keep analytic comparisons and explain that inside tests need a closed mesh.
findings.verification: Source-review the statement against MeshBvh.closestPoint/contains/raycastAll; replay the printed ray/nearest/inside answers. No performance benchmark is required for the qualified claim.
